Description

The active RAF dimer at the plasma membrane phosphorylates MEK1 and MEK2 on two serines of their activation loop, S218 and S222 in human MEK1 and S222 and S226 in MEK2 (S217 and S221 in the rabbit MEK1 studied first) [1, 2]. With RAF1, only the doubly phosphorylated MEK1 was detected, even when little of it was phosphorylated, which suggests that the first phosphorylation limits the rate and the second follows at once [1]. Whether both are needed is not settled: replacing either serine of human MEK1 by alanine abolished its activation by RAF [2], whereas in the rabbit enzyme replacing either one by glutamate was enough for maximal activity [1]. MEK is bound to BRAF already in the autoinhibited complex and stays on each kinase of the active dimer, and phosphorylation releases it [3].

References

  1. Alessi DR, Saito Y, Campbell DG, Cohen P, Sithanandam G, Rapp U, et al. Identification of the sites in MAP kinase kinase-1 phosphorylated by p74raf-1. EMBO J. 1994;13(7):1610-9. PMID: 8157000. doi: 10.1002/j.1460-2075.1994.tb06424.x.
  2. Zheng CF, Guan KL. Activation of MEK family kinases requires phosphorylation of two conserved Ser/Thr residues. EMBO J. 1994;13(5):1123-31. PMID: 8131746. doi: 10.1002/j.1460-2075.1994.tb06361.x.
  3. Park E, Rawson S, Li K, Kim BW, Ficarro SB, Pino GG, et al. Architecture of autoinhibited and active BRAF-MEK1-14-3-3 complexes. Nature. 2019;575(7783):545-550. PMID: 31581174. doi: 10.1038/s41586-019-1660-y.
